title.narrative: PERFORMANCE-BASED PARTNERSHIP SCHEME FOCUSING ON QUALITY PROGRAMMING, UNDERSTANDING CHANGE AND RESULTS FOR POOR HOUSEHOLDS AND COMMUNITIES

description.narrative: In Matabeleland South, the S4Nut programme helped supported households strengthen climate‑resilient food systems, with 94% increasing production and 90% achieving acceptable food consumption through drought‑tolerant crops, home gardens and nutrition‑focused learning. Private‑sector partners supported value addition and access to inputs, helping families expand market opportunities. Disaster‑risk partnerships benefiting 26,238 people enhanced community preparedness, enabling earlier action to protect crops, livestock and nutrition during climate‑related shocks. In Harare, the Graduation Approach enabled 1,576 vulnerable people to improve food access and income stability through cash transfers and tailored livelihood support. . Supporting diverse, nutrition‑sensitive production and improved nutrition practices, in a context where recurrent droughts, rising food prices and limited dietary diversity continue to leave vulnerable families at high risk of hunger and malnutrition.
